subject: Default purge exclusions — concrete examples for customer FAQ
messages:
From: Alice Mason <alice.mason@brightbank.com>

Cc: BrightBank Security Team <security@brightbank.com>

Subject: Clarify default purge: concrete examples needed

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the chat earlier. As part of BrightBank's procurement checklist we need a short, concrete list of what Redwood means by the 'default purge' (the standard retention behavior before any special residency or hold). The procurement folks want examples that they can show auditors. Specifically can you confirm the default behavior for:
- Streamed tokens in interactive sessions
- Final generated outputs (full responses)
- Prompt history / customer-supplied content
- KV cache and ephemeral session state
- Attachments uploaded during a session (e.g., PDFs)
- Backups and disaster recovery snapshots

Also: are there automatic exceptions (e.g., for backups, billing records, legal holds)? If you can point me to a one-page breakdown or attach a matrix we can include in the RFP that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Mason

alice.mason@brightbank.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify default purge: concrete examples needed

Hi Alice — thanks for the detailed list. I pulled together a concise explanation below and attached a simple matrix (retention-example-matrix.xlsx) and our SOC2 evidence bundle (SOC2-evidence.pdf). High level first, then the examples you asked for.

High level: by default we retain minimal artifacts required for billing, fraud detection, and platform health for a short configurable horizon (default 45 days for interactive request/response records in the hosted plan). Generated outputs and prompts are considered 'captured artifacts' if a customer enables request logging; otherwise streamed tokens are ephemeral and not stored beyond processing unless the session is explicitly saved. We make the following distinctions:

- Streamed tokens: ephemeral by default. Streams are buffered for immediate delivery; unless 'save_session' or logging is enabled, streams are not persisted.
- Final generated outputs (responses): stored by default for 45 days when request-logging is enabled; if logging is not enabled they are not recorded.
- Prompt history / customer-supplied content: treated as customer-provided data and captured only if request-logging is on or if the customer stores conversation transcripts. Default hosted behavior is to treat prompts as transient unless logged.
- KV cache / ephemeral session state: ephemeral and only lives in-memory on the serving node; it is not persisted to long-term storage.
- Attachments uploaded during session: attachments referenced by a session (e.g., PDF uploads) are stored in object storage if the customer chooses to persist them; otherwise we stream them through the runtime and do not permanently store.
- Backups / DR snapshots: backups of system metadata are retained according to our infra runbook and are not part of the customer-visible request/response horizon; they are encrypted and kept for a longer window to support disaster recovery (we document this in the SOC2 artifacts).

Automatic exceptions: billing records, audit logs required for accounting, and legal hold requests are retained beyond the default purge. Also, if a customer uses Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployments and configures different policies, the retention horizon may differ. We note those exceptions in the attached matrix.

I'm adding Kimberly on legal/privacy and Marissa on product to make sure I captured the nuance for auditors. If you'd like, we can replace the high-level bullets in the attachment with BrightBank-specific phrasing.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt

Hannah/Alice — quick legal addendum.

1) Residency and contractual overrides: Customers in the EU or on Dedicated/Private plans frequently contract for longer or shorter retention windows; the default described above is our hosted-default and does not override a contractual residency/retention clause.

2) Backups & immutable storage: Our disaster recovery backups are treated as a separate control plane and are not searchable or accessible as request/response artifacts; they exist to restore service and are retained per the DR policy (longer than 45 days). For SOC2 auditors we provide a mapping of the types of backup artifacts vs. their retention in SOC2-evidence.pdf.

3) Legal holds & e-discovery: If BrightBank issues a legal hold, we escalate to Legal/Support — those records are isolated and excluded from automated purge until clearance.

4) PII / encryption: PII that customers transmit is encrypted at rest and in transit. Our retention guidance recommends customers enable redaction or tokenization for highly sensitive fields; we can include recommended redaction examples in the matrix.

I'll let Marissa confirm the product wording for the attachment and then Hannah can send the customer-facing version.

Kimberly Park

Alice — thanks for the ask. I attached an updated retention matrix with BrightBank-specific phrasing and three concrete example rows (copied below) that auditors find helpful. If this looks good I'll send as a single-page PDF for your RFP pack.

Example rows (for auditors):
1) Interactive chat where logging = off: streamed tokens are ephemeral, final outputs are not stored. Default purge/no capture.
2) Interactive chat where logging = on: prompts + final outputs captured to hosted logs, default retention 45 days, then auto-purged. Billing/audit metadata retained longer for accounting.
3) Attachment upload (PDF) during session with explicit save: attachment stored in object storage, retention follows customer-configured policy; default hosted retention of stored artifacts is 90 days unless otherwise contracted.

Next steps: confirm whether BrightBank wants the PDF to reference our SOC2 section numbers (we included them in the matrix) and whether you want a short signature line from Kimberly about legal holds.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if you want a walkthrough.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Data Lifecycle
Redwood Inference
